newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho rebel police charged with treason.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho rebel police charged with treason.

text.p: Thirty two rebel Lesotho policemen, linked to an attempted mutiny earlier this year in the tiny southern African mountain kingdom, on Thursday were formally charged with high treason.
Lesotho's chief magistrate Letsela Mapetla read out the charges to the accused in the Maseru Magistrate's Court and committed them for trial in the Lesotho High Court at a date to be announced.
The February crisis, which was quickly crushed by the Lesotho army, began when eight junior policemen accused of murdering three of their colleagues seized control of police headquarters in Maseru.

Among the charged was the mutineers' leader, Phakiso Molise, who fled to South Africa after the army crackdown in order to seek political asylum. His request was refused and he was deported back to Lesotho at the end of April.
The accused arrived in court without incident, but were escorted by soldiers wielding AK-47 assault rifles.
